index.title: Start here
index.body:
This is a small example vault. A few ordinary notes that show what Myne can do, and nothing here is special: edit, rename, or delete any of it.

- [[{{markdown}}]] shows how plain text becomes formatting
- [[{{tasks}}]] gathers checklists into one place
- [[{{links}}]] connects notes and sorts them with tags
- [[{{makeItYours}}]] clears all of this in one step

Seen enough? Right-click the **Getting started** folder in the sidebar and choose Delete. The notes move to Trash, so you can bring them back if you change your mind.

markdown.title: Writing with Markdown
markdown.body:
Myne writes plain Markdown and shows the result as you type.

## The basics
Make a word **bold** or *italic*, or drop in `inline code`.

## A list
- One item
- Another item
  - A nested one

## A quote
> Small notes, kept for years, beat big notes you never write.

## A table
| Shortcut | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Cmd/Ctrl + B | Bold |
| Cmd/Ctrl + K | Add a link |

## Some code
```
console.log("hello from Myne")
```

When you are ready, head back to [[{{index}}]].

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.body:
Any line that starts with `- [ ]` is a task. Myne collects every open task from across your notes into one Tasks view, so nothing gets lost between notes.

- [ ] Read [[{{markdown}}]]
- [ ] Add a task of your own
- [ ] Try one with a due date 📅 2030-12-31
- [x] Create your vault

Check a box here, then open the Tasks view in the sidebar to watch the list update.

Back to [[{{index}}]].

links.title: Links and tags
links.body:
Type `[[` to link to another note. Links go both ways: open [[{{index}}]] and you will see this note under its backlinks, and the graph draws a line between them.

Add a #tag anywhere and Myne files the note under it in the tag tree. This note is tagged #example and #getting-started, so open the tag tree in the sidebar to find it.

Your turn: link this note to [[{{tasks}}]], or invent a tag of your own.

makeItYours.title: Make it yours
makeItYours.body:
This is your vault now. These notes are only a starting point, so change anything, or clear them and begin fresh.

To remove the whole example, right-click the **Getting started** folder in the sidebar and choose Delete. Everything moves to Trash together, and you can restore it from there if you want it back.

When you are ready, press Cmd/Ctrl + N to make a new note and start writing.

welcome.body:
Welcome to Myne, your private space to think and write.

Everything you save here is encrypted and stays on your device. Your **password** and **recovery phrase** are the only keys to it, so keep them somewhere safe. If both are ever lost, no one can get your notes back, not even us.

**You can link notes to each other.** Type `[[` and Myne offers the notes you already have; pick one and it becomes a link. The note you linked TO shows where the link came from, in its own backlinks panel, so a set of notes is something you can follow in either direction.

This is just a regular note, so make it your own. Edit it, rename it, or delete it whenever you like, and add new notes as your ideas grow.

To learn more about Myne, visit https://myne.md

network.residualPayment: If you pay for hosted sync, the payment and your account can still be linked to you. Tor changes where the connection comes from, not the billing trail.
network.residualScope: On desktop this covers your sync traffic and your remote AI provider requests. Mobile has no Tor routing yet, so its provider requests go direct. Nothing else on this device goes through Tor.

It is effective on Windows 10 (May 2020 Update) and later; macOS and Linux have no system API for it, so it cannot block capture there. Where it does work, what it hides the window from includes remote-desktop software and screen magnifiers, which is why this way out exists.

briefing.heading: Before you create your vault
briefing.intro: Myne encrypts your notes so that only you can open them. Three things follow from that. Read them, then continue.

no-email.ackLabel: I understand there is no email recovery.
no-email.statement: There is no email recovery. There never will be.
no-email.why: We never ask for your email, so there's no reset link and no account for support to unlock. This isn't a missing feature. It's the guarantee. Email recovery would mean we could read your notes, and Myne is built so we can't.

no-store.ackLabel: I understand Myne can't recover my password.
no-store.statement: Your password unlocks your vault. We don't store it.
no-store.why: Your password is the input to the key that decrypts your notes. It never leaves this device, and nothing on our servers can reproduce it. That's what keeps your notes private, and why we can't reset it for you.

phrase-backup.ackLabel: I understand my recovery phrase is the only backup.
phrase-backup.statement: Your recovery phrase is your only backup.
phrase-backup.why: If you forget your password, the 24-word recovery phrase is the one way back in. {{lostBothSecrets}} Write the phrase down and keep it somewhere safe.

unsupported.mobileTitle: Open Myne's app on this device
unsupported.handoff: Myne's desktop app (macOS, Linux) and mobile app (Android) have no such limit, and an app you install stays installed: if you kept the file you downloaded, it is still on your disk to compare against the hash Myne publishes for the current release. Nothing does that comparison for you. No Windows build and no installable iOS build are published yet. A web page is re-sent to your browser every visit, and your browser checks nothing on it.

reason.desktop-form-factor: Myne in the browser is built for a desktop computer. It needs the memory and the input a phone or tablet browser cannot give it. On this device the Myne app is the better client anyway: it is faster, it works offline, and it keeps your notes when the browser clears its storage.
reason.webassembly: This browser does not support WebAssembly, which the encryption core runs on.
reason.wasm-memory-headroom: This browser cannot reserve the ~336 MB of memory the vault's key derivation needs. Phone and tablet browsers generally cannot; that limit is set by the vault itself and cannot be lowered for one device without making the vault unreadable everywhere else.
reason.worker: This browser does not support Web Workers, which the vault's storage and encryption run inside.
reason.opfs: This browser does not provide private local storage for web apps, so there is nowhere to keep your vault between page loads.
reason.opfs-sync-access-handle: This browser's private local storage is missing the synchronous file access the vault needs to write safely.
reason.web-locks: This browser does not support the lock that keeps two tabs from writing to one vault at the same time.
reason.crypto-getrandomvalues: This browser does not provide a cryptographic random-number source.
